text:
anya: quick note — bringing up honeycomb-mini (multilang) quantized to int6 on staging. ran our short-tail recall suite and seeing a weird pattern :thinking_face:

devon: what pattern?

anya: recall@1 dropped from ~0.62 (float16 baseline) to ~0.53 after int6 quant. recall@5 also down but less so. cluster tightness seems different in t-SNE — small queries collapse into a few dense blobs.

kai: do you have the eval command/params you used?

anya: ran the usual eval: ```python eval_embeddings.py --model honeycomb-mini-int6 --dataset webqa-shorttail --index hnsw --ef_search 64 --topk 10 --normalize True```

miriam: did you rebuild the index after quantizing? we need to re-index, otherwise distance geometry might mismatch.

anya: yes re-indexed from scratch on staging nodes. also tested without L2 normalize and got slightly different numbers: recall@1 bumped to 0.56 but clustering worse.

devon: any per-dim clamp or per-channel scaling applied during quant pipeline? int6 is sensitive to range outliers.

anya: used uniform symmetric quant with global scale. we haven't tried per-channel.

kai: can you paste the small summary stats? mean pairwise cosine, silhouette scores, etc.

anya: short summary:
- baseline float16: recall@1 0.62, recall@5 0.84, silhouette 0.21, mean pairwise cos 0.28
- int6 global: recall@1 0.53, recall@5 0.79, silhouette 0.12, mean pairwise cos 0.31
- int6 + L2norm(False): recall@1 0.56, recall@5 0.80, silhouette 0.09

miriam: silhouette drop is worrying — means cluster separability reduced. could be quantization causing axis-aligned distortion. per-channel might help. also consider re-fitting whitening/centering on quantized vectors.

devon: agree. pipeline idea: (1) per-channel scale (ASymmetric?) (2) re-fit PCA/whitening after quantized encode (3) try bias correction / calibration using 5k anchor set.

anya: I can run per-channel symmetric int6 and re-fit whitening. how long for a full anchor pass? ~30 mins?

ops-bot: scheduled job eval-anchor-5k-honeycomb-int6 at 2026-03-21T14:12:00Z (job id: jb-9421).

kai: also check short queries length distribution — embedding magnitude might be correlated with token count. if short queries are low-norm after quant, they collapse. try length-bucketed quant calibration.

anya: good point. I see mean norm for <=6 tokens dropped 18% post-quant, whereas >20 token queries unchanged.

miriam: then try per-bucket scale factors or add a tiny bias term after quant to restore norms. could be simpler than full per-channel.

devon: additionally, test index settings: ef_construction=200, M=32 may amplify dense blobs. rebuild HNSW with M=48 and ef_search 128 for recall comparison. sometimes graph params interact with quant noise.

anya: queued experiments:
1) per-channel int6 + re-fit whitening (anchor-5k calibration)
2) per-length-bucket scale correction + L2norm on encode
3) rebuild HNSW with M=48, ef_search 128
4) baseline float16 re-run for parity check

kai: what's success threshold? restore recall@1 to within 5% relative of baseline (i.e., >=0.59) and silhouette >0.18.

anya: noted. I'll run 1) and 2) today and post numbers.

miriam: if 1/2 don't help, fallback is int8-perchannel for production — cost delta is small but may be needed. Also document everything for release notes.

anya: raw commands I'm running (for reproducibility):
```
# encode + quantize per-channel
python encode.py --model honeycomb-mini --quantize int6 --per_channel True --anchor_set data/anchor-5k.jsonl --out embeddings/honeycomb-int6-perchan.npy
# fit whitening on quantized embeddings
python fit_whitening.py --emb embeddings/honeycomb-int6-perchan.npy --out transforms/honeycomb-int6-whiten.npz
# build index
python build_index.py --emb embeddings/honeycomb-int6-perchan.npy --index hnsw --M 48 --ef_construction 200 --out index/honeycomb-int6-m48
# eval
python eval_embeddings.py --index index/honeycomb-int6-m48 --queries data/webqa-shorttail-queries.jsonl --topk 10
```

devon: sweet. tag me when results land and also dump per-bucket norm histograms.

anya: will do. first run (per-channel) finished: recall@1 0.595, recall@5 0.82, silhouette 0.19, short-query norm drop reduced to 6%.

miriam: nice, that's within threshold for recall and silhouette. any regressed queries we should inspect?

anya: pulled top 50 regressions — many are paraphrase edge cases and named entities normalization. were already borderline. attaching sample: /staging/artifacts/honeycomb/int6/perchan/regressions_sample.csv

kai: next steps: run full 50k holdout sweep and sanity-check multilingual parity for non-English short-queries. if stable, we can promote to canary.

miriam: also add automated anchor-based calibration step to the quant pipeline to avoid future surprises. small PR pls.

anya: filing PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/521 (WIP)

devon: awesome. thanks for the quick pivot. :rocket:
